en: So at this point, I'm pretty much done with
this example here, but there are 2 remaining
features or
things you should know about HTMX.
And the first thing you should know is that
HTMX also offers you some configuration
options.
Now, again, as always, the official docs are
a great place to learn about all the
options, but in the end, the idea is that
HTMX offers some options
you can set up to achieve a certain default
behavior which you might not have otherwise.
For example, if you find yourself setting
hx-swap to outerHTML all the time and you
therefore want that as a default instead of
innerHTML, which it normally would be, you
could achieve that by overriding the default
HTMX configuration.
And there are 2 ways of doing that.
One way
is to go into your main.js file
and then there you'll have access to a
globally available HTMX variable which is
created by HTMX. Now you can console.log
that to
see what's inside of it.
And if you do that, you'll see that it's an
object which has a nested config object
which has all the options you can set.
And for example, here you also see that
defaultSwapStyle, which is set to innerHTML
out of the box.
Now we could change this here and set
HTMX.CONFIG.defaultSwapStyle,
and you must make sure that you got the
casing right and that you got no typo.
And then you can set this to
outerHTML here, for example.
With that, if you save that and you reload,
you'll see that this is now the default that
is assumed.
Now as a result, our app would actually
break here because I'm relying on this not
being the default. But if you had an app
where you need a different default, this is
how you could set it up.
An alternative way of configuring HTMX is to
do it via HTML.
You can go to your head section of the page
that's currently active.
And then there you can add a meta
element
and give it a name of HTMX-config because
that is a name HTMX will be looking for.
And then there as a content, you can set up
your configuration.
For that, you must pass some JSON data. To
content and hence I'll wrap this with
single quotes because I need the double
quotes to wrap my keys.
And then here we could also set up the
default swap style and set it to
outerHTML, for example.
So that would then be the HTML approach of
configuring HTMX.
With that added, if I save that and reload,
you'll see that in config,
This is now again the default swap style
and therefore again, this app here breaks.
But if you need to configure something, that
is an alternative way of doing it.
Here, however, I don't need that and
therefore I'll remove it.
